The proposed answer is incorrect, because the inner radius formula it uses is wrong.

**Where the error is.** Each chord $A_iA_{i+k}$ lies at distance $\cos(\pi k/n)$ from the center. The 24 chords have normal directions spaced $2\pi/n$ apart. Two adjacent chord lines therefore meet at radius

$$r=\frac{\cos(\pi k/n)}{\cos(\pi/n)},$$

not $\dfrac{\cos(\pi k/n)}{\cos(\pi(k-1)/n)}$ as the solution claims.

**Correct computation.** With $n=24$:

- $r_1=\dfrac{\cos(9\pi/24)}{\cos(\pi/24)}$
- $r_2=\dfrac{\cos(11\pi/24)}{\cos(\pi/24)}$

The radius ratio is

$$\frac{r_1}{r_2}=\frac{\cos(9\pi/24)}{\cos(11\pi/24)}=\frac{\sin(3\pi/24)}{\sin(\pi/24)}=3-4\sin^2(\pi/24)=1+2\cos(\pi/12).$$

Since $\cos 15^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}$, this gives

$$\frac{r_1}{r_2}=1+\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{2}\approx 2.932.$$

The area ratio is the square of this, about $8.60$.

The proposed answer is $3+\sqrt6-\sqrt2-\sqrt3\approx 2.30$, which does not match.

VERDICT: REJECT
